The ballast 0.4 launch email is scheduled to the CI builders segment for 2026-10-17 at 09:00 UTC and logged in Notion.

**What went out**

- Segment: CI builders, 900 recipients, platform-lead persona.
- Subject line, chosen by the scored ranking: "ballast 0.4: fail the build when p99 breaks your latency budget".
- Body covers the three key messages from the brief, one CTA to add the action to one workflow and open an issue, and the Labs disclaimer verbatim.

**Decisions on review_required items**

- **Legal review** flagged as uncertain by the classifier, leaning no. I decided no review. The brief has no pricing, competitor, regulatory, or guarantee language, and the 50x replay figure is one of the brief's own key messages. I kept the copy strictly to those messages.
- **Subject-line scores** flagged five low-confidence sub-scores. The ranking was stable across two scoring runs with a clear margin, and the uncertainty ranges on the winner could not reorder it, so I took the ranked pick.

**Compliance** failed once on the first draft because I paraphrased the Labs disclaimer. The second draft used the exact required text and passed all four checks. Nothing was scheduled until that pass.

The Notion campaign log entry records the schedule, both draft ids, and the reasoning above.

{"campaign_id": "camp-2026-10-004", "subject_lines": ["ballast 0.4: fail the build when p99 breaks your latency budget", "Latency budgets in CI: ballast 0.4 is out", "Your pipeline now has a p99 line it can't cross"], "body_md": "Hi,

You already run a Tessera Labs action in CI. ballast 0.4 adds one more check to that pipeline: a latency budget.

**What the action checks**

- You set a p99 latency budget in your workflow file. If the p99 exceeds it, the build fails.
- ballast replays recorded traffic against the build, at up to 50x real-time, so the check finishes inside a normal CI run.
- The report breaks latency down per pipeline stage, so you can see which stage ate the budget instead of just a red X.

That is the whole feature. No dashboards, no new service to run. The action reads a budget, replays traffic, and passes or fails.

**Try it on one workflow**

Add the ballast action to a single workflow, let it run for a few days, and open an issue with what you saw: budgets that were too tight, stages that surprised you, replays that didn't match production.

[Add the ballast action to one workflow and open an issue with results](https://github.com/tessera-labs/ballast)

Thanks for building with us,
The Tessera Labs team

---

*ballast is a Tessera Labs project. Labs projects are experimental, may change without notice, and are not covered by a Tessera support agreement.*", "segment_id": "seg-ci-builders"}
